articleBody:
Before bringing in a finish carpenter to install baseboards, window casings, or decorative wainscoting in your bathroom, use this checklist to make sure your space is fully prepped and you hire the right professional.

- [ ] Inspect existing drywall and subfloor moisture levels — Carpentry should never be installed over damp drywall or leaking subfloors.
- [ ] Verify that primary plumbing and tile work are 100% complete — Finish trim sits against finished tile and needs completed surfaces for proper reveals.
- [ ] Confirm your exhaust fan operates properly — Adequate room ventilation protects newly installed wood trim and painted finishes from excessive steam.
- [ ] Measure total linear footage for baseboards, door casing, and crown — Accurate measurements allow contractors to order proper material lengths with minimal seams.
- [ ] Select moisture-appropriate trim materials — Choose cellular PVC or sealed wood rather than moisture-absorbing paper-faced MDF in wet splash zones.
- [ ] Check wall straightness along floor and ceiling lines — Uneven walls require custom scribing and solid backing rather than excessive caulk.
- [ ] Clarify who handles caulking, hole-filling, and final painting — Confirm whether your finish carpentry quote includes turn-key finish painting.
- [ ] Verify contractor licensing, references, and BBB accreditation — Partner with a recognized, experienced contractor who understands bathroom wet areas.

How to Use This Checklist
Review these items prior to your on-site consultation. Completing these checks ensures accurate quotes and seamless project execution. To discuss your bathroom finish carpentry project in the Denver metro area, call Abraham Becerra at HH Remodeling LLC at 303-505-0866.
